explanation: Belt grips, open-hand slaps, shoves and lifts are all legal. Hair pulling and closed-fist punches are fouls; otherwise a wrestler loses by leaving the ring or touching down.

claims.text: In sumo, deliberately pulling an opponent's hair is a foul that loses the bout.
Gripping the opponent's belt (mawashi), open-hand slaps, pushing and lifting the opponent are legal techniques in sumo.
Punching with a closed fist is also a foul in sumo.
A sumo wrestler loses by leaving the ring or by touching the ground with any part of the body other than the soles of the feet.

evidence.restatement: Pulling the hair is a kinjite, a forbidden move, and loses the bout.
Belt grips, open-hand thrusts and slaps, pushing and lifting the opponent are all legal sumo techniques.
Striking with a closed fist is also a kinjite.
A wrestler loses by leaving the ring or touching the ground with anything but the soles of the feet.
Pulling an opponent's hair (the topknot) is one of sumo's prohibited acts (kinjite) and loses the bout by disqualification.
Belt grips, open-hand slaps, pushes and lifts are standard legal sumo techniques.

claimResults.note: True in general terms. Two narrow variants are prohibited acts: gripping the front flap of the mawashi over the groin, and clapping both ears at once. See the ambiguity note.

evidence.restatement: Closed-fist punches are prohibited acts in sumo.
A rikishi loses by leaving the ring or by touching the ground with anything other than the soles of the feet.

issues.note: Two distractors have narrow prohibited variants (the front groin flap of the belt; a double ear clap), so a sumo expert could quibble. 'Gripping the belt' and 'open-hand slaps' are legal as written, and pulling hair is the clear foul, so the key stands. The explanation's 'all legal' could say 'generally legal'.

editor.reason: Both checks pass; all four claims are standard risk and confirmed at certain in both checks. B's note (narrow prohibited variants: the front flap of the belt, a double ear clap) leaves the three distractors legal as written and hair pulling the one clear foul, so no change.
